operations.name: Al McSurely

expected.name: Al McSurely
expected.description: Al McSurely was a civil-rights and anti-poverty organizer working in eastern Kentucky. Pike County officers raided the home he shared with his wife Margaret on August 11, 1967, seized their books and papers, and arrested both of them under Kentucky’s sedition law. McSurely spent one week in the Pike County jail before obtaining release on bail. A federal court later held the state sedition statute unconstitutional, and the charges did not produce a conviction.

operations.source: Primary Kentucky Photo Archive, Herald-Leader photograph of Alan McSurely speaking at University of Kentucky, published September 13, 1967: https://kyphotoarchive.com/2015/09/23/civil-rights-worker-alan-mcsurely-1967/ . Identified speaker isolated by exact rectangular crop (900,420,1250,980) from 2048x1376 reproduction; no generative editing. Source and credit in CREDITS-batch892.md.

operations.name: Kiyoshi Okamoto

expected.sentence:
Four years at the U.S. Penitentiary, Leavenworth; the convictions were reversed on appeal in 1945.

Verdict as recorded: Yes — convicted by a federal jury in Cheyenne in October 1944 and sentenced to four years at Leavenworth; the Tenth Circuit overturned the conspiracy convictions in 1945.

Charges as recorded: Conspiracy to counsel draft evasion — for leading the Heart Mountain Fair Play Committee, which urged imprisoned Nisei to refuse induction until their constitutional rights as U.S. citizens were restored.

operations.source: Primary National Archives judgment and commitment against Kiyoshi Okamoto dated November 2, 1944, NAID292820, described at https://text-message.blogs.archives.gov/2022/06/07/japanese-american-internment-and-resistance-at-heart-mountain/ . Court historical timeline confirms sentencing day and trial judge Eugene Rice: https://justiceforall.ca2.uscourts.gov/reenactments/heart-mountain-draft-resisters/the-heart-mountain-draft-resisters-timeline/ . Individual museum profile confirms July 20, 1944 arrest: https://heartmountain.org/draft-resisters-hub/okamoto-eugene-kiyoshi/ . Existing DOB year1889 conflicts with museum1888, preserved and flagged. Earlier administrative internment not automatically assigned as start of criminal imprisonment; reversal not actual release.
